newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Cruz Blanca splits into four units.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Cruz Blanca splits into four units.

text.p: Shareholders of Chilean services company Cruz Blanca SA voted to split the company into four different companies and to sell one of those divisions, company officials said.
The four separate firms to be created in the breakup were Cruz Blanca Prevision y Seguros, CB Capitales, CB Transportes e Infraestructura and CB Inversiones Inmobiliarias.

The move allows Cruz Blanca to spin off the first of those four, a life and health insurance unit, to the Hurtado Vicuna family which last month offered shareholders 93-95 cents a share to buy 51 percent of it.
The spinoff will allow Cruz Blanca's owners, the Cruzat group, to concentrate their business on financial services, public works projects and real estate.

CB Capitales, a financial services outfit, will post about $2.6 million profits in 1997 and will be in a good position to broaden its business in mutual funds, mortgage bonds, factoring and stock brokering, said CB Capitales general manager Juan Braun.
